howItWorks.title: How the Bubbles Work
howItWorks.description1: Popping bubbles keeps your hands and attention busy. Meanwhile, the mind turns away a little from anxious thoughts: this is the principle of distraction.
howItWorks.description2: Each popped bubble gives a small visual and sound response, and a simple gesture to repeat. Many people find this repetitive movement helps release restlessness.
howItWorks.description3: It is a short, effortless break, useful when anxiety makes a longer exercise like breathing or relaxation difficult.

focusRedirection.title: Shifting attention
focusRedirection.description: Attention moves to the gesture and the sensation rather than to worry.

sensoryFeedback.title: Instant feedback
sensoryFeedback.description: The sound and animation of each bubble make the gesture pleasant to repeat.

nervousSystemCalm.title: A repetitive gesture
nervousSystemCalm.description: Repeating a simple gesture helps release restlessness.

science.title: What Studies Say
science.description: No study has tested virtual bubbles themselves. They rely on distraction, a method mostly studied in children during painful medical procedures.
science.bottomLine: distracting yourself with a simple gesture can help you get through a moment of anxiety. It is a short-term aid that complements other techniques without replacing them.

distraction.title: Distraction during needle procedures in children
distraction.who: Children and adolescents aged 2 to 19 during blood tests, vaccines or IV insertion (up to 30 trials and 2,800 children).
distraction.what: Distraction methods (games, videos, toys…) compared with usual care.
distraction.result: Distracted children felt less pain and less distress.
distraction.caution: Low-quality evidence, in children and during a medical procedure: it cannot be applied directly to anxiety in adults.

whenToPractice.title: When to Practice
items: When you feel restless energy or need to keep your hands busy during anxiety
During waiting periods or before stressful events when you need distraction
When anxious thoughts are racing and you need to break the cycle
As a quick reset between tasks to release built-up tension

whatYoullNotice.title: What You Might Notice
items: The simple pleasure of each popping bubble
Attention gradually turning away from anxious thoughts
Less restlessness and urge to move
A slightly calmer state after a round

posture.title: Rhythm
posture.description: Pop bubbles at your own pace—fast for energy release, slow for methodical calming. There's no right speed.

environment.title: Sound
environment.description: The pop sound adds to the experience. Use it where you're comfortable or mute if needed in quiet spaces.

consistency.title: Repetition
consistency.description: Multiple rounds are fine. Reset and repeat as many times as you need to fully release tension.
